We waterproof leaking roofs, flat roofs, parapets, damp walls, balconies and showers for homeowners in Pretoria and Gauteng, and in Betty's Bay to Gansbaai in the Overstrand. Ask for a free assessment and written quote.

A leaking roof usually shows up after a Highveld storm: a stain on the ceiling, a drip into a cupboard, or water tracking along a beam. Damtech waterproofs house roofs in Pretoria and the rest of Gauteng, including tiled roofs, concrete slabs and metal sheets.

We look at the roof covering, flashings, outlets and any old coating before we recommend a repair or a new membrane. You get a free assessment and written quote. We do not publish a rate per square metre, because every roof is different.
Flat concrete roofs and box gutters hold water when outlets block or the falls are too flat. Parapet walls crack at the corners, and water then runs down inside the plaster.

We prepare the slab, open failed laps, and waterproof the parapet upstands, flashings and outlets so rain is carried off the roof instead of into the wall. Depending on the roof, that may be a torch-on bitumen membrane or a liquid-applied system; the written quote names the system and why it suits your roof.

Damp walls are not always a roof leak. Rising damp leaves a tide mark low on interior walls, blistered paint and a musty smell, often where the damp-proof course has failed or garden soil sits against the plaster.

We trace whether the moisture is rising from the ground, coming through a retaining wall, or entering from a leaking pipe or roof. The written quote says what we will treat and what still needs a builder or plumber.
Balconies and shower floors leak into the room below when the membrane under the tiles has failed, or when the waste and door threshold were never sealed.

We inspect the screed, outlets and upstands. Where the tiles have to come up, we say so before any work starts. The same free assessment and written quote covers balconies, planters and shower floors.
Not every wet ceiling has a hole you can see. Water can travel along a slab, a conduit or a parapet and appear metres away from the entry point.

We check the roof, walls, balconies and plumbing penetrations, and we tell you if the leak is a waterproofing failure or something a plumber should fix first. Leak detection is part of the assessment, not a separate priced product on this page.
Damtech also works from Betty's Bay in the Western Cape, so we assess and waterproof homes in Betty's Bay, Kleinmond, Hermanus, Gansbaai and the surrounding Overstrand.

Coastal houses fail differently from Highveld houses. Most rain falls in winter, often driven sideways by strong wind, and salt air corrodes metal flashings, fixings and gutters. Wind-driven rain frequently enters through parapets, window heads and wall junctions rather than the roof covering, so we inspect the walls and flashings as well as the roof before recommending a system.
HOW IT WORKS
From the first photo to the written quote, you know what we found and what we recommend before any work starts.
Phone, WhatsApp or the quote form. Tell us where the house is and send photos of the stain, roof or damp wall.
We inspect the roof, parapets, damp walls, balcony or shower and find where the water is getting in.
You receive a free assessment and written quote that sets out the work, the system we recommend, and the warranty terms.
We prepare the surface, install the agreed system and leave the area weather-tight. Warranty terms are confirmed in your written quote.

Tell us about the leaking roof or damp wall and we will arrange a free assessment and written quote. Up to 10 years supplier-backed material warranty where stated in the quotation, plus 12 months Damtech workmanship warranty from practical completion (unless otherwise agreed in writing).

/Dam Liners & Dam Linings in the Western Cape
HDPE Dam Lining Installation — Western Cape
Wine, fruit and livestock farms from the Boland to the Overberg rely on Damtech dam linings to keep scarce summer water in farm dams for irrigation and stock.

Western Cape agriculture operates under some of the country’s tightest water scrutiny. Winter cold fronts fill dams between June and August; summers are dry, windy and unforgiving on open water. Farmers in Stellenbosch, Franschhoek, Grabouw and the Swartland cannot treat seepage as acceptable losses — many dams sit on sandstone-derived soils and weathered granite that drink water year-round without a visible leak on the surface.
Damtech operates from Betty's Bay in the Western Cape and mobilises across the province for dam lining, waterproofing and water-storage projects. This is an operating base — not a walk-in office.
LOCAL CONDITIONS

Mediterranean rainfall dominates: wet winters, dry summers. Berg wind events raise evaporation on east-facing dams in the Boland. Snow melt from peaks contributes late-spring flow in some catchments, but licensed abstraction caps mean stored winter volume must last through berry and grape ripening. Climate variability since 2015 has made lining projects a standard capital item rather than a discretionary repair.
SITE FACTORS

Table Mountain Group sandstones and granite saprolite produce shallow, stony profiles on slopes — dam basins often need benching and geotextile before HDPE. Alluvial floors in valleys offer better natural sealing but still benefit from lining when irrigation security is critical. Wind-blown sand accumulates in dam corners; maintenance access after installation helps keep outlets clear.
WATER USE

Vineyards use deficit irrigation schedules tied to dam level — seepage forces either curtailment or expensive alternate sources during véraison. Apple and pear orchards in Grabouw run sprinklers and micro systems from farm dams that must survive the February heat. Livestock farms on wheat stubble country store drinking water for sheep through dry months when pans evaporate completely.
SECTORS

Wine and juice grapes, deciduous fruit, olives, livestock and equine properties dominate lining demand. Rural lifestyle estates line ornamental and fire dams. Packhouses and cold stores occasionally need waterproofed roofs and lined balancing ponds — secondary to farm dam work but part of integrated site water plans.
STORAGE

The economic case for HDPE is retaining licensed winter allocation inside the dam footprint. Damtech has completed large installations in Stellenbosch and Grabouw, documented in our projects section, which farmers can use as references when planning for their own catchments.

Steel tanks where dam expansion is constrained by licence or terrain

/western-cape-dam-liners/.mobileVisibleText: Home / Services / Dam Liners & Dam Linings in the Western Cape HDPE Dam Lining Installation — Western Cape Dam Liners & Dam Linings in the Western Cape Wine, fruit and livestock farms from the Boland to the Overberg rely on Damtech dam linings to keep scarce summer water in farm dams for irrigation and stock. Request a Quote Contact Damtech Western Cape agriculture operates under some of the country’s tightest water scrutiny. Winter cold fronts fill dams between June and August; summers are dry, windy and unforgiving on open water. Farmers in Stellenbosch, Franschhoek, Grabouw and the Swartland cannot treat seepage as acceptable losses — many dams sit on sandstone-derived soils and weathered granite that drink water year-round without a visible leak on the surface. Western Cape service area Damtech operates from Betty's Bay in the Western Cape and mobilises across the province for dam lining, waterproofing and water-storage projects. This is an operating base — not a walk-in office. +27 82 853 1026 LOCAL CONDITIONS Climate & Seasonal Rainfall Mediterranean rainfall dominates: wet winters, dry summers. Berg wind events raise evaporation on east-facing dams in the Boland. Snow melt from peaks contributes late-spring flow in some catchments, but licensed abstraction caps mean stored winter volume must last through berry and grape ripening. Climate variability since 2015 has made lining projects a standard capital item rather than a discretionary repair. SITE FACTORS Soils & Ground Conditions Table Mountain Group sandstones and granite saprolite produce shallow, stony profiles on slopes — dam basins often need benching and geotextile before HDPE. Alluvial floors in valleys offer better natural sealing but still benefit from lining when irrigation security is critical. Wind-blown sand accumulates in dam corners; maintenance access after installation helps keep outlets clear. WATER USE Irrigation & On-Farm Water Use Vineyards use deficit irrigation schedules tied to dam level — seepage forces either curtailment or expensive alternate sources during véraison. Apple and pear orchards in Grabouw run sprinklers and micro systems from farm dams that must survive the February heat. Livestock farms on wheat stubble country store drinking water for sheep through dry months when pans evaporate completely. SECTORS Agriculture, Mining & Industry Wine and juice grapes, deciduous fruit, olives, livestock and equine properties dominate lining demand. Rural lifestyle estates line ornamental and fire dams. Packhouses and cold stores occasionally need waterproofed roofs and lined balancing ponds — secondary to farm dam work but part of integrated site water plans. STORAGE Water Storage Needs The economic case for HDPE is retaining licensed winter allocation inside the dam footprint. Damtech has completed large installations in Stellenbosch and Grabouw, documented in our projects section, which farmers can use as references when planning for their own catchments. LOCAL SERVICES Damtech Services in This Area Large-area HDPE farm dam lining PVC lining for ponds and estate water features Steel tanks where dam expansion is constrained by licence or terrain Liner inspection, patch repair and outlet refurbishment Damtech dam lining and water storage installations. CASE STUDIES Related Projects Dam lining and water storage projects completed by Damtech in similar conditions.
